name: Lagged non-mechanistic history baseline (ARX) for the nested FGF2-ERK forecast comparison
reason: Reviewer item R2: M reweights B3 samples by all past observations while O uses three exponential summaries, so M versus O changes both mechanism and history representation. A lagged baseline with a training-selected window tests whether the B3 increment still adds once input and reporter histories are represented directly.
context: Post hoc robustness analysis on inspected roles, using the data roles, forecast origins, future-command features, scores and B3 increments of configs/nested_forecast_protocol.json.

models.A: current-state set C + reporter lags y(t - 2k) and command lags u(t - 2k), k = 1..L frames; reporter lags before the first frame repeat the first observation, command lags before the origin are zero (pre-stimulation)

selection.fixed_roles: window and penalty jointly minimize the condition-equal validation MSE after fitting on train; sigma of the B3 increment as selected for M on validation
selection.lopo: for each held-out protocol group: sigma on the training groups; window and penalty by inner leave-one-group-out over the training groups; the held-out group enters no standardization, selection or fit

reports: condition-equal RMSE of A and A+M for every role and horizon beside P, C, O, M and H
per-condition counts for A versus O, A+M versus A and A+M versus H
phase-wise RMSE on tests A-C and the next-command window per condition with rows, cells and origins
corrected LOPO RMSE of A and A+M per fold with the B3 prior use
primary_question: A+M versus A at 10 min on test A and across the corrected LOPO folds: does the B3 increment add predictive value once input and reporter histories are represented directly?
reporting: All comparisons reported whatever their direction; no significance testing (no independent-day replicates).
